description:
Overview
Colony House is a grand, three-story historic mansion situated on a hill overlooking the Township. In direct ideological opposition to the individualist family structures of the Town, Colony House functions as a free-spirited, communal sanctuary. Led by Donna Raines, the residents share all resources, sleep in communal wards, grow their own food, and live by a philosophy of 'living in the present moment.' It is heavily secured with a Talisman, allowing the large group of survivors to sleep safely at night—until its defenses are catastrophically breached.

Key Features
The Greenhouse: Located on the mansion's grounds, this glass dome serves as the primary cultivation hub for the community's crops, representing their hope for sustainable survival.

The Communal Ward: The large dormitory rooms where dozens of residents sleep side-by-side, reflecting the house's radical rejection of traditional nuclear family units.

The Foyer and Grand Staircase: The central architectural space of the mansion, frequently used for communal dining, meetings, and parties.

Notable Lore
The Choosing Ceremony: Colony House is one of the two core factions that newcomers must choose between at the Choosing Stone. It offers a communal lifestyle of shared resources, whereas the Town offers individual family homes and a structured, rule-bound community.

The Season 1 Breach: The mansion becomes the site of one of the show's most horrific tragedies. A resident named Kevin becomes infatuated with a female Creature named Jasmine, opening a second-story window to let her in. Jasmine brutally eviscerates Kevin, opening the doors for a horde of monsters to enter. The resulting massacre claims the lives of numerous residents, forcing Donna, Boyd, and others to make a chaotic and bloody retreat to the Town center.

Fatima and Ellis's Wedding: Colony House is a place of rare joy in Season 2 when Fatima and Ellis (Boyd's son) are officially wed on the grand porch, representing the community's refusal to let the darkness destroy their humanity.

Located on the grounds of Colony House, this glass structure is the town’s primary source of cultivated food. It represents survival and the fragile hope of the residents, though it is often a target for sabotage or monster-driven psychological warfare.

Overview
Located directly adjacent to the main grounds of Colony House, this small, secure outdoor shed is used by Donna Raines and her residents to store heavy equipment, tools, and communal supplies. Following the psychological strain and escalating conflicts among the survivors in Season 2, it is strictly repurposed as a secure lockup for firearms to keep weapons out of the communal house.

Key Features
The Weapons Locker: A designated, locked space inside the shed where Colony House guards store all firearms and ammunition away from the general populace.

The Vulnerable Threshold: While small enough to be protected by a Talisman, its physical distance from the main building makes walking to it a tense, high-stakes task when tensions are high or night is falling.

Notable Lore (Season 2)
The Firearms Lockup: Following a chaotic and sleepless night plagued by deaths and paranoia, Donna orders the guard Matthias to gather all the firearms from the main house and permanently lock them in the shed, stating she does not want guns circulating among the panicked residents.

The Murder of Matthias: While Matthias is finishing up inside the shed, a deeply unhinged Reggie approaches him under the guise of helping. Driven by madness and grief over the loss of his wife Paula, Reggie violently cuts Matthias' throat inside the shed, killing him instantly to steal a shotgun and wage his own war against the Town.

Repurposed from the Town’s former school building, the Clinic functions as Fromville's sole medical facility. Medical supplies are severely scarce, with the vast majority being painstakingly stripped or salvaged from an ambulance—affectionately nicknamed "T.R.O.Y."—that became permanently trapped in the Township. The main floor features makeshift cots for patients, while the secure basement is used for high-risk patients. It also serves as the personal living quarters for Kristi Miller, the third-year medical student acting as the Town's doctor.

Key Features
The Ambulance ("T.R.O.Y."): Permanently parked directly outside the Clinic, this Type II van-ambulance is the primary lifeblood of the town's medical operation, acting as the original source for critical supplies, medicine, and saline.

The Secure Basement: A lower storage area that initially provided a safe, enclosed nightly refuge for vulnerable residents before becoming a site of absolute horror.

Notable Lore
The Basement Massacre (Season 1): The Clinic became the scene of a devastating tragedy when Sara Myers suffered a psychological break under the influence of the voices. Sara intentionally left the building's door open at night, letting the Creatures inside. The monsters brutally eviscerated Nurse Gina and Kenny's father, Bing-Qian Liu, shattering the town's fragile sense of security.

The Autopsy of a Monster (Season 2): Following the death of the "Smiley" Creature, its corpse was brought to the Clinic. Operating under extreme dread, Kristi, Kenny, and Boyd performed an unprecedented autopsy on the monster, uncovering that its internal organs were completely withered and dried—save for a mysterious, toxic fluid.

The Reunion (Season 2): The building bridges the world before and the nightmare of the Town when a passenger bus arrives, unexpectedly carrying Kristi’s fiancée, Marielle (a pediatric nurse), who joins the Clinic staff.

Overview
Located on the isolated outskirts of the Town, the Root Cellar is a subterranean storage bunker. On the surface, it appears to be a dusty, unused shelter that desperate residents occasionally use to hide from the Creatures after dark. Beneath that facade, however, it is one of the most volatile supernatural vectors on the map—acting as a vault for multi-generational trauma, terrifying localized hallucinations, and a gateway to the darkest corners of the forest's curse.

Key Features
The Main Vault: A concrete storage area containing old furniture, including a deceptive armoire that serves as a visual playground for terrifying, localized illusions.

The Secret Back Room: Discovered by Elgin behind a heavy cabinet, this hidden room contains an overturned cot and an ancient, decayed skeleton. It functions as the primary haunting ground for the ghost of the Kimono Woman.

The Subterranean Hatch: A concealed trapdoor hidden beneath the dirt floorboards. This hatch bypasses the surface entirely, serving as a direct elevator shaft down into the deepest, monster-filled chambers of the Tunnels.

Notable Lore
The Tragedy of Victor’s Childhood: This cellar is the origin point of Victor's lifelong trauma. As a boy, his mother hid him and his sister Eloise here before going to find the Farway Tree. Eloise ran out after her, leaving a frozen-with-fear Victor alone. When he emerged the next morning, the entire population of the Town had been slaughtered.

Jade's First Visions (Season 1): While exploring, Jade Herrera opened the cellar's armoire and witnessed a terrifying apparition of a bloody corpse crushed by a boulder. When he fell back in fear, he spotted the mysterious, recurring geometric symbol painted directly onto the cellar ceiling.

The Farway Tree Transit (Season 1): During the chaotic assault on Colony House, Victor used a Farway Tree to instantly teleport Julie Matthews directly into the safety of this cellar to survive the night.

The Abduction of Fatima (Season 3): Manipulated by visions of the Kimono Woman, Elgin transformed the hidden back room into a prison, kidnapping a pregnant Fatima. He barricaded her inside and desperately fed her jarred blood, believing the unborn child was a miracle meant to save them all.

The Pod Birth & The Hatch (Season 3): The cellar becomes the ultimate site of body horror when Fatima goes into labor. Assisted by the Kimono Woman, she gives birth to a grotesque, fleshy sac-like pod. The Kimono Woman takes the pod down the hidden floor hatch into a subterranean chamber, where the long-dead "Smiley" Creature horrifyingly hatches from it right in front of an investigating Sheriff Boyd.

Overview
Located in a neutral clearing between the Town and the forest, this large, flat rock is where newly arrived survivors must make a permanent, defining choice. After spending their first night surviving a monster attack, newcomers are brought here by Sheriff Boyd Stevens and Colony House leader Donna Raines to choose how they want to live out their entrapment: under the laws and structures of the Town, or the communal, free-spirited isolation of Colony House.

Key Features
The Two Baskets: During the ceremony, two distinct baskets are placed on the stone. One contains a traditional Talisman (representing the Town's focus on individual family units and rules), and the other contains white flowers (representing Colony House's philosophy of shared resources and communal living).

The Ultimatum: The choice made at the stone is absolute. Once a resident selects a path, they are expected to stay in their designated zone, drawing a harsh cultural line through the middle of the community.

The Audience: Ceremonies are typically attended by residents from both sides, who watch from a distance to see who will join their respective factions, creating a high-stakes, tense atmosphere for the terrified newcomers.

Notable Lore
The Matthews Family Split (Season 1): The ceremony became a major flashpoint when the Matthews family arrived. While Jim, Tabitha, and Ethan chose the Town, their teenage daughter, Julie, rebelled and chose Colony House. This fractured the family immediately upon their arrival, forcing them to live under completely different survival conditions.

Ideological Battleground: The stone highlights the deep philosophical rift between Boyd (who believes in order, routine, and finding a way home) and Donna (who believes the town is a permanent trap and that survival requires living for the present moment without rigid rules).

A Rite of Passage: The ceremony is designed to force newcomers to accept reality. By making them choose a survival method, Boyd and Donna strip away the denial of being "lost" and force them to face the rules of the environment.

Overview
The designated worship building in the Town, featuring a main floor for sermons and a basement used for storage. Directly adjacent to the building is the Town's graveyard. Following the death of Father Khatri, the Church has evolved from a place of spiritual guidance into a somber space where the dead are brought, prepared for burial, and laid to rest.

Key Features
The Graveyard: The adjacent resting place where victims of the Creatures—including Lauren, Meagan Pratt, Nathan, and Tian-Chen Liu—are buried during formal funeral services.

The Storage Basement: A critical narrative flashpoint. It is used by Father Khatri to secretly hide and interrogate Sara Myers after her crimes, and later serves as her temporary shelter and a confrontation site for suspicious residents.

Notable Lore
The Unwritten 74th Book (Season 1): Inside the basement, Father Khatri shares his theory with Sara that the Town's residents are living through a dark, unwritten 74th book of the Bible, suggesting they were chosen for a specific purpose.

The Sins of the Town (Seasons 1 & 2): The Church is where Boyd and Khatri fiercely debate the ethics of "The Box" punishment. Later, an exasperated Boyd uses the empty Church to scream at God, demanding to know if their suffering is just a joke.

Preparation of the Dead (Season 3): Following the brutal murder of Tian-Chen Liu, Jade and Kristi use the Church to meticulously clean and prepare her body, granting her dignity before the community holds her funeral.

The Boy in White's Message (Season 3): Victor reveals that as a child, he entered the Church basement and witnessed the Boy in White speaking to Christopher. The Boy delivered a cryptic message: "The answers to the end are in the beginning," explaining that murdered children lay on stones where roots became Farway Trees. This revelation is what originally drove Victor's mother to leave him and look for the tree.
These are standardized residential units within the Township. In your Godot project, these can serve as modular environmental assets that define the "suburban nightmare" aesthetic of the town center

The Blue House is one of the town's most important transition points. It serves as a primary residence for new arrivals who choose to stay in the town rather than at Colony House. It is a place of forced adaptation, where strangers are often thrust together to form makeshift families in order to survive their first few nights.

Overview
The Star Magic Motel Pool is a bizarre, unfinished landmark on the edge of the Township. While the inground concrete swimming pool and its accompanying "Star Magic Motel" sign were completely built, the actual motel building itself was never constructed. The empty, dry pool is unused by the residents and contains an overturned truck at the bottom—a vehicle that Boyd recalls belonged to former residents named Danny and Shay.

Key Features
The Motel Sign: A standalone vintage sign marking a motel that doesn't exist, serving as a strange piece of evidence regarding how the Town's impossible infrastructure was constructed.

The Overturned Truck: A rusted vehicle resting inside the dry pool basin, serving as a grim visual anchor that triggers Boyd's anxieties about the people he has lost over the years.

The Concrete Wall Cairn: A makeshift, solemn memorial erected out of stones inside the pool to cover up a horrific structural anomaly.

Notable Lore (Season 3)
Henry's Observation: Upon arriving in the Township, Victor's father, Henry, stands by the sign and points out the eerie contradiction of the location to Ethan Matthews: there is a sign and a pool, but absolutely no motel.

The Bottle Tree Disaster: The pool becomes the site of a gruesome supernatural accident when a resident named Dale panics and steps through the Bottle Tree. Instead of safely teleporting to the Lighthouse, the portal’s physics glitch, fusing Dale directly inside the solid concrete wall of the motel pool.

The Mercy Killing Attempt: As Dale is slowly crushed and suffocated to death inside the solid concrete, a devastated Boyd prepares to shoot him to end his misery, though Dale succumbs to his injuries just before the trigger is pulled. Boyd uses this horrific sight to warn the rest of the townspeople about the extreme dangers of blindly messing with the Farway Trees.

Donna's Memorial: Unable to chip Dale's body out of the structure, Donna Raines uses heavy stones to build a cairn directly over his exposed remains inside the concrete wall, transforming the unfinished pool into a permanent graveyard.

Overview
Located within the main Township, this two-story house is the family home of the Lius. As one of the most stable and tightly-knit family structures in the community, the house acts as a beacon of warmth, tradition, and sanctuary. It is protected by a Talisman at night, allowing the family a fragile sense of domestic normalcy amidst the surrounding terror.

Key Features
The Kitchen: The heart of the home, where Tian-Chen Liu routinely prepared home-cooked meals for her family and guests, keeping traditional cooking practices alive to preserve her family's heritage.

The Living Room: A communal space where Kenny, his mother, and his father gathered, trying to maintain a normal household routine despite the omnipresent threat outside their windows.

Notable Lore
The Burden of Dementia (Season 1): The home was a place of immense emotional strain before the Talismans were implemented. Kenny’s father, Bing-Qian Liu, suffered from advanced dementia, making it incredibly difficult for Kenny and Tian-Chen to keep him quiet and safe during the terrifying nights when they had to hide in underground root cellars.

A Sanctuary of Grief (Season 1): Following the brutal murder of Bing-Qian in the Clinic basement by the Creatures, the home shifted into a space of profound mourning for Kenny and his mother, testing their resilience and forcing Kenny to step up heavily as the Town's Deputy.

The Mother's Loss (Season 3): The house suffered its ultimate tragedy in Season 3 following the horrific execution of Tian-Chen Liu by the Creatures. Her absence leaves the home completely empty, leaving Kenny to navigate the house alone as a silent monument to the family he lost to the Town.

Tom’s Bar (The Distillery)
The Bar is a converted roadside service station that serves as the town’s primary social hub and moonshine distillery. Originally established and managed by Tom, a former philosophy professor, the building has shifted from a place of grim escapism into a makeshift research center. Since the town lacks commercial alcohol, the bar is famous for its "potato vodka," a harsh moonshine brewed in a rudimentary still in the back.

Recent Events and Current Status
The Bar is currently in a state of mourning and transition following the death of its owner. During the events surrounding the collapse of the Matthews' house, Tom was trapped in the wreckage while trying to help. He was ultimately killed by the monsters during the night, leaving the establishment without its original caretaker.

Since Tom's death, the location has been effectively commandeered by Jade Herrera. No longer just a place to drink, the bar has become Jade’s base of operations for his increasingly obsessive attempts to solve the town's puzzles.

the Barn is a critical, high-stakes location on the outskirts of town. Once a simple place for livestock (like the cow, Alma), it has evolved into the most traumatic landmark in the series—a site used by the entities of the forest for extreme psychological and physical torture.

Key Details for Your Interactive Map
Location: Situated on the edge of the residential area, close to the forest line. Its isolation makes it a death sentence for anyone caught there after sunset.

The Livestock Massacre: In the most recent events, the monsters pivoted from hunting humans to psychological warfare. They broke into the Barn and slaughtered the town's animals—not for food, but to systematically starve the residents and break their spirits.

The Death of Tian-Chen: This is a defining tragedy for the site. While trying to protect the remaining livestock, Boyd and Tian-Chen (Kenny’s mother) were trapped. The monsters tied Boyd up and forced him to watch as they slowly tortured and executed Tian-Chen, turning the Barn into a place of profound grief for the Stevens and Liu families.

The Discovery of Jim's Body: In a sadistic twist, the Man in Yellow used the Barn to shatter the Matthews family. After Jim went missing, his mutilated body was left hanging upside down inside the Barn. The monsters specifically staged this so that his children, Julie and Ethan, would be the ones to find him, turning a place that Ethan once considered a "safe" play area into a house of horrors.

Overview
The Sheriff’s Office (historically the Town’s post office) serves as the absolute command center for law, order, and strategic defense in Fromville. Managed by Sheriff Boyd Stevens and Deputy Kenny Liu, this highly fortified building houses the town's administrative files, a temporary holding cell, and Boyd’s personal office. It is a vital sanctuary secured by a Talisman, frequently used to shelter displaced residents, contain dangerous secrets, and coordinate town-wide emergencies.

--

Key Features

The Map of Arrivals: Located inside the office, this is a master map pinned with the origins and roads of every resident trapped in the Town, serving as a bleak reminder of their shared, impossible geography[cite: 29, 30].
The "Nights Without Incident" Sign: A prominent chalkboard outside the station used to track the town's days of safety. Following devastating events, the count is manually reset to zero or one, reflecting the fragile state of peace[cite: 20].
The Holding Cell: A makeshift jail space used to lock up unruly residents or temporarily house survivors when other safe houses collapse[cite: 16, 18].
Boyd's Office Desk: A central hub where critical supplies—including an extra revolver kept in the drawer and Father Khatri’s personal stash of alcohol—are stored[cite: 70, 86, 87].

--

Notable Lore by Season

Season 1: Tragedy and Transition
The Death of Father Khatri: Following a chaotic breach at the clinic, Boyd brings a fatally wounded Father Khatri to the steps of the station[cite: 11, 13]. Khatri tragically dies outside the doors while he and Boyd recite the Lord's Prayer[cite: 12, 15].
The Colony House Refuge: After a devastating creature attack at Colony House, the station becomes a crowded temporary shelter[cite: 16]. The psychological toll peaks when a resident named Eric commits suicide inside the station overnight, resetting the town's safety sign to day "1"[cite: 20, 21].

Season 2: Psychological Breaking Points
The Bus Arrival Siege: During the chaotic night the Grand Rapids bus arrives, Ellis and Fatima seek shelter inside the station[cite: 34, 35]. From the windows, they are forced to watch helplessly as stranded passengers outside are slaughtered by the Creatures[cite: 37, 38, 39].
Sara’s Russian Roulette: Confined to the station, a guilt-ridden Sara Myers faces an aggressive confrontation with Kenny over her role in his father’s murder[cite: 57, 65, 67, 68]. In a moment of extreme psychological distress, Sara loads two bullets into Boyd's gun, points it at Kenny, and then pulls the trigger against her own head in a desperate game of chance[cite: 70, 74, 75].

Season 3: Fractured Leadership and Dark Truths
The Livestock Rescue: Following the attack on the Barn, an injured Boyd uses his office to recover and argue with Donna over his controversial choice to risk human lives to save the town's wandering livestock[cite: 78, 89, 90, 91].
Officer Acosta's Disarming: A panicked, newly arrived police officer named Acosta ransacks the office looking for her weapon[cite: 95, 102]. Boyd fiercely asserts his authority, returning her gun only after completely unloading the bullets, proving that normal badges mean nothing in the Township[cite: 105, 106, 108].
Boyd's Parkinson's Confession: After experiencing severe tremors while searching for a missing Fatima, a breaking Boyd forces his son Ellis to sit down for a drink[cite: 114, 115, 117]. He finally confesses his secret diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, which he had been hiding since before his first trek into the forest[cite: 118].
The Taunting Voices: While poring over maps to find Fatima, Sara arrives at the office with a terrifying message from the entities: the voices have returned, taunting Boyd that Fatima is close but he will be too late to save her[cite: 128, 129, 130, 131].

The Bus is the most significant addition to the town’s geography since the arrival of the Matthews family. It is a Grand Rapids Runner tour bus that brought 25 new passengers to the town at the start of Season 2, signaling a major escalation in the town's population and the monsters' aggression.

The "Siege" Site: On its first night in town, the bus became a death trap. Two elderly passengers stayed on board and were brutally killed by Smiley (the creature Boyd eventually killed).

The Newcomer Conflict: The bus represents the moment the town's delicate balance broke. To prevent the driver from leaving and leading everyone to their deaths, Donna was forced to shoot out the bus tires, effectively trapping the new residents forever.

Randall’s Fortress: For much of Season 2 and 3, the bus served as the isolated home of Randall. After he refused to follow Colony House's rules, Donna "exiled" him to the bus. He fortified it, even moving seats to the roof to act as a lookout point and a place to fly his drone.

The Night of the Cicadas: The bus was a central location during the "Music Box" curse. Randall suffered horrific hallucinations of cicadas while trapped inside, and it was nearly the site of his death before the curse was broken.

The "Safe" Sanctuary: In Season 3, the bus briefly became a place of refuge. When the monsters released the livestock and attacked the town, Sara Myers managed to get Julie and Ethan Matthews to the bus, where Randall ushered them inside for safety.

Overview
Located within the main Township, this two-story house served as the primary residence for the Matthews family after they completed the Choosing Ceremony. Originally structured to offer the newly arrived family a sense of stability and individual privacy, the house became a central hub for engineering escape plans. However, its structural integrity was completely tied to the town's supernatural forces, leading to its catastrophic destruction in Season 2.

Key Features
The Dig Site / Basement: The most critical area of the house. Driven by a desperate need to find out where the town's impossible electricity comes from, Tabitha and Jim dug a massive hole through the basement floor, eventually breaching into the subterranean network where the Creatures sleep.

Ethan’s Bedroom: A space upstairs where Ethan mapped out his theories regarding the "Quest" and interacting with his visions of the Boy in White.

Notable Lore
The Family Divide (Season 1): Upon moving in, the house immediately reflected the trauma of the Choosing Ceremony. While Jim, Tabitha, and Ethan inhabited the home, their teenage daughter Julie chose to live at Colony House, fracturing the family unit from their very first day in Town.

The Basement Breach (Season 1): Following days of excavation, Tabitha finally broke through the basement floor, only to have the ground collapse beneath her. She fell directly into the Cave Entry/Tunnels, forcing Victor to rescue her from the dormant monsters while Jim desperately tried to dig her out from above.

The Catastrophic Collapse (Season 2): In a direct supernatural retaliation against Jim and Tabitha's attempts to investigate the town's infrastructure (via the radio tower and the basement hole), the entire house structurally failed. The building collapsed into a massive pile of rubble, trapping Jim and a newly arrived bus passenger, Brick, beneath the debris and killing Brick in the process.

Overview
A classic, mid-century American chrome and teal diner located at the absolute center of the Town. More than just a restaurant, the Diner acts as the literal heart of the community. It is where Fromville's residents gather to eat, start, and end their days together with communal meals. Because of its central location and large size, it functions as the town's primary food depository, as well as a storeroom for keeping the left-behind personal belongings of deceased residents.

Key Features
The Counter & Kitchen: Long a symbol of comfort, this area was fiercely managed by Tian-Chen Liu, who poured her heart into feeding the community until her tragic death in Season 3. Following her loss, the bus driver, Bakta, stepped in to cook and manage the daily operations.

The Tabletop Jukebox: A piece of vintage Americana that occasionally triggers and turns itself on automatically without anyone touching it. To the longtime residents, it is a known quirk of the town's impossible electrical grid.

Notable Lore
The Ominous Seizure (Season 1): The Diner is the site of a terrifying supernatural manifestation. While observing the newly arrived Matthews family during dinner, words painfully carve themselves into Sara Myers’ arm: "KILL THE BOY." Immediately following the message, Sara collapses into a severe seizure, signaling her deep and forced connection to the entities.

Victor's Warning (Season 1): During a community breakfast, Victor approaches Ethan Matthews inside the Diner to warn him that the forest trees are moving four inches closer to the town. He also identifies Ethan's "Boy in White" from a childhood sketch, confirming to himself that the entity has returned.

The Shift in Grief (Season 3): Following the brutal murder of Tian-Chen Liu by the Creatures, the Diner shifts into a state of mourning. Jade Herrera and Kristi Miller prepare her body at the church while the townspeople gather near the Diner to mourn the loss of the woman who sustained their daily survival.

Overview
Located within the main Township, this modest residential home belonged to the siblings Nathan and Sara Myers upon their arrival in Fromville. While it functions as a standard, Talisman-secured safe house at night, the home is a dark focal point in the town's history. It is where Sara's intense psychological torment began, ultimately transforming their sanctuary into the launching pad for a series of horrific internal betrayals.

Key Features
The Sibling Living Space: Before the town's peace was shattered, the house was a place where Nathan carefully looked after his deeply traumatized sister, trying to establish a quiet routine to help her cope with the reality of their entrapment.

The Living Room / Kitchen: The domestic setting where Sara first began experiencing the agonizing physical and auditory manifestations inflicted upon her by the mysterious entities of the forest.

Notable Lore
The Genesis of the Voices (Season 1): It was inside this home that Sara Myers first began hearing the distinct, intrusive voices of the town's unseen forces. The entities used her vulnerability to feed her information they shouldn't know, eventually forcing her into a state of psychological compliance under the promise that it would get everyone sent home.

The Death of Nathan (Season 1): The home became a scene of absolute tragedy after Sara succumbed to the voices' demands to kill Ethan Matthews. When Nathan discovered her dark intentions, a frantic struggle ensued inside the house. In his desperate attempt to stop his sister from becoming a monster, Nathan was accidentally killed when Sara inadvertently threw him into the path of a closing door/blade, stripping Sara of her only moral anchor.

An Abandoned Monument: Following Nathan's death and Sara's subsequent exposure, isolation, and eventual confinement in the church, the house stands as a chilling, semi-abandoned reminder to the rest of the Township of how easily the forces in the woods can corrupt the people inside the walls.

Abby’s Grave
Abby’s Grave is a haunting, secluded landmark in the world of FROM, serving as a central point of grief and mystery for the Stevens family. Unlike the other residents of the town who are buried in the communal graveyard, Abby is interred in a remote clearing deep within the woods. The site is marked by a simple, weathered wooden cross, often adorned with fresh wildflowers left by her husband, Boyd, who visits to "talk" to her during moments of extreme crisis.

Architecturally, the location is significant due to its proximity to a prehistoric Stone Circle—a "Stonehenge-like" arrangement of ancient slabs that suggests the site may hold spiritual or supernatural power beyond just a final resting place.

Overview
Discovered by Sheriff Boyd Stevens and Sara Myers during their high-stakes expedition into the deep woods, this specific Bottle Tree stands far beyond the town's explored parameters. While it visually resembles the Farway Bottle Tree used by Tabitha, it does not function as a physical teleportation gateway. Instead, this ancient tree acts as a historical time capsule for Fromville, decorated with dangling glass bottles that contain handwritten chronological evidence of the town's centuries-old cycle.

--

Key Features

The Clinking Branches: Dozens of glass bottles hung by strings from the branches, which sway in the wind and create a distinct clinking sound that guides travelers to the clearing.
The Cursive Artifacts: Unlike the digits found in the gateway tree, the notes inside these bottles contain specific years meticulously written out in cursive.
The Spider Territory Border: This tree marks the immediate physical boundary where the deep forest begins to transition into the territory of massive, unseen arachnid entities.

--

Notable Lore (Season 1)

The Edge of the Map: As Boyd and Sara trek deeper into the forest than any resident has ever dared to go, they follow a mysterious clinking noise to this clearing. Sara is stunned to find the tree, noting that Boyd himself previously stated that this territory was completely unreachable.
Sara's Seizure: The moment Boyd reaches up to knock one of the glass bottles down to inspect it, a massive wave of supernatural feedback hits the clearing. Sara experiences an excruciating, violent seizure and collapses to the ground, forcing Boyd to abandon his investigation to tend to her.
The 1864 Reveal: After setting up their tent nearby to let Sara recover overnight, Boyd reveals that he successfully retrieved a slip of paper from one of the fallen bottles. The note reads exactly "1864", dropping the first major historical confirmation to the survivors that previous groups of travelers have been trapped in the Township for centuries.

The Brundles is a small, scenic lake located near Colony House. It is the primary recreational spot for the town, characterized by a small wooden dock and a collection of toys left there by residents. The name "The Brundles" was given to the lake by the inhabitants of Colony House long before most of the current characters arrived.

Factual Events at the Brundles (Season 1-3)
Julie’s Introduction: Fatima uses the lake to help Julie adjust to the town, emphasizing that the community tries to maintain a sense of beauty despite the horror.

Elgin’s Arrival: Elgin’s first request in town is to see the water, confirming his connection to the "dream" he had on the bus.

The "Lake of Tears" Theory: While Ethan and Elgin both discuss a "Lake of Tears" from stories and visions, it has not been confirmed in the show that the Brundles is that lake. Many characters (and fans) suspect a connection, but as of the most recent episodes, the Brundles remains a relatively "quiet" location compared to the Barn or the Clinic.

Jade’s Floating Scene: Jade is seen floating in the Brundles while deep in thought, using the quietness of the water to process his mathematical theories and the symbols he sees

Overview
A somber, sprawling clearing filled with the rusted remains of vehicles belonging to the Township's former residents. While it looks like an ordinary junk pile, it is actually a monument to the town's tragic history. After the Creatures wiped out the original population when he was a child, Victor painstakingly moved every car here so he wouldn't have to look at them while walking the empty streets.

Key Features
The Station Wagon: Victor’s mother’s old vehicle, which serves as a makeshift safe box where Victor hid his sister Eloise's childhood drawings.

The Rock Line: A distinct geographical boundary in the clearing. The vehicles parked beyond these rocks predate Victor’s arrival in the 1970s, proving the town's trap has been active for generations.

Christopher’s Car: The specific vehicle belonging to a former resident who went mad after obsessed with the mysterious symbols, eventually leading to the town's mass slaughter.

Notable Lore
The Origin of the Symbols: Victor brings Jade here to fulfill a bargain, revealing that the town's descent into madness began when Christopher started seeing the symbols and stopped smiling.

The Lighthouse Revelation: While sorting through the drawings in the trunk with Tabitha, Victor recovers his deeply repressed memories of his sister, Eloise, and uncovers a drawing of a Lighthouse—the place their mother died trying to reach.

A Sanctuary for Grief: In Season 3, overwhelmed by the impossible arrival of his father, Henry, Victor retreats to this graveyard to hide and process the trauma of his past before being comforted by Sara.

Overview
Hidden deep within the forest brush, this rocky opening is the primary gateway to the Tunnels—a sprawling, subterranean labyrinth directly beneath Fromville. Unbeknownst to the town's residents for years, this pitch-black network is where the Creatures sleep during the day. Entering the cave before nightfall is a death wish, as it exposes the intruder directly to the monsters in their dormant state.

Key Features
The Cave Paintings: The walls surrounding the entry passages are covered in eerie, primitive drawings. Victor reveals that these paintings were actually created by the Creatures themselves, hinting at a dark, ancient history.

The Hoarded Artifacts: Deep past the threshold lies a disturbing graveyard of human belongings. The Creatures don't just sleep here; they hoard the souvenirs of their victims, including suitcases, clothing, and old toys like the creepy ventriloquist dummy.

The Root Symbol: In the deepest chambers, the overhead tree roots intertwine to form the exact mysterious symbol that haunts Jade, acting as a natural skylight into the cave.

Notable Lore
The Basement Collapse (Season 1): Tabitha Matthews literally drops into this location after digging through her basement floor. She is rescued by Victor, who was instructed by the Boy in White to wait for her at the cave's edge and guide her safely past the sleeping monsters.

The "Anghkooey" Kids: The mouth of the cave acts as a spiritual hotspot. Tabitha is swarmed here by the spirits of the Ghoulish Children chanting "Anghkooey," a vision that triggers a severe physical toll (a bloody nose) and pushes her to find the Lighthouse.

Jade’s Spool of Thread (Season 2): Determined to decode his visions, Jade hitches a spool of thread to a tree outside the Cave Entry, mapping his way into the heart of the darkness. It is here that he witnesses the Ghoulish Children on stone altars beneath the root symbol.

Overview
Located on the main road leading into the Township, this is the exact intersection where the modern timeline of Fromville was shattered. It is the site of the unprecedented double-crash involving the Matthews' RV and Jade luxury car. In the history of the Town, two new vehicles arriving on the exact same day was an unheard-of anomaly—a catastrophic event that shattered the town's long-standing period of stability and triggered a dangerous new shift in the environment.

Key Features
The Matthews' RV: A large recreational vehicle that served as the temporary, highly vulnerable safe house for the Matthews family on their terrifying first night.

The Impaled Car: Jade's overturned sports car, which bore the brunt of the initial collision and left its passengers severely injured.

Notable Lore
The Two-Car Omen (Season 1): According to the town's lore—and later confirmed by the voices to Sara—the simultaneous arrival of two separate cars is a historic omen. The last time two cars arrived on the same day, it resulted in a mass slaughter where almost every resident in the Township was wiped out.

The First Night Siege: Following the crash, Ethan Matthews was left pinned inside the RV by a metal bracket through his leg, making it impossible to move him before sundown. Sheriff Boyd Stevens stayed behind, pinning a Talisman to the RV's window. This marked the first time a Talisman was successfully tested and proven to work inside a mobile vehicle, protecting the family while the Creatures circled outside all night.

The Casualties: While Jim, Tabitha, Julie, Ethan, and Jade survived the crash and the subsequent night, Jade's friend Tobey was taken to the clinic with severe injuries, where he was ultimately murdered by a compromised Sara before he could fully process the town's reality.

Overview
Located far out in the deepest, uncharted parts of the forest, the Dungeon is a supernatural location that exists outside of Fromville's conventional space and time. It physically manifests as a crumbling, roofless stone tower or castle ruin. It is a place of immense suffering and ancient malice, serving as a literal prison where mysterious forces torture captives—both living and dead. It is accessible only through specific, supernatural gateways like the Farway Trees.

Key Features
The Stone Wall Shackles: Heavy iron chains bolted directly into the stone walls. These cuffs were used to permanently imprison captives, keeping them alive indefinitely through supernatural means despite severe starvation and dehydration.

The Invisible Rope Ladder: The only physical way out of the roofless structure. It cannot be seen from the ground, requiring someone from above to lower it down to anyone trapped inside the ruins.

The Music Box: A sinister, supernatural artifact that plays a haunting melody. It serves as the auditory anchor for the malevolent entity that controls the Dungeon, acting as a timer for its psychological torture.

Notable Lore
The Discovery of Martin (Season 2): After climbing through a Farway Tree, Boyd Stevens is instantly teleported inside the Dungeon. There, he finds Martin—a frail, elderly man chained to the wall who claims to have been trapped there for decades. Martin warns Boyd that the Creatures are just "the tip of the spear" and that there are far worse things hiding in the woods.

The Blood Infection: Before dying, Martin begs Boyd to kill him. When Boyd hesitates, Martin slashes Boyd's arm and passes a swarm of mysterious, parasitic worms under Boyd's skin, warning him that "my blood is your blood now."  The Ruin Paradox: When Boyd returns to the exact location later with his son Ellis, the intact stone tower is gone. In its place are only ancient, decayed stone ruins that look centuries old, proving the Dungeon shifts its appearance or exists in a completely different time period.

The Cicada Curse: The Dungeon acts as the epicenter of a nightmare curse. When the Music Box plays, a swarm of supernatural cicadas is unleashed into the Town. The insects burrow into residents like Paula and Reggie, killing them from the inside out or trapping their minds back inside the Dungeon's torture chamber. Boyd eventually destroys the entity by returning to the ruins and smashing the physical Music Box.

Overview
Farway Trees are massive, ancient trees scattered throughout the forest that defy the laws of physics. They function as unpredictable, localized teleportation portals. When an object or a person is placed inside the hollow opening of a Farway Tree’s trunk, they are instantly transported to another location within the Fromville landscape.

Key Features
The Hollow Trunk: The physical gateway. Anything dropped or pushed into the opening disappears completely, re-emerging somewhere else.

Random Teleportation: Traveling through a Farway Tree is highly volatile. Unlike a standard door, a tree typically sends travelers to a completely random coordinate in the woods—with a few rare exceptions.

The "Through the Looking Glass" Physics: Items dropped down the tree fall upwards or outwards at their destination, operating on a logic that Victor describes as being similar to a fairy tale.

Notable Lore
Victor and Ethan's Expedition (Season 1): Victor introduces a fascinated Ethan Matthews to the tree's anomalous properties. To demonstrate how it works, Victor drops a rock into the trunk, and they watch it instantly drop from the sky a short distance away. Victor explains that while most destinations are random, some trees can have fixed endpoints if you know how to use them.

Boyd's Desperate Escape (Season 2): While trapped in the forest at night with Sara Myers as the Creatures close in, Sara pushes Boyd into a Farway Tree to save his life. The tree teleports Boyd directly inside the narrow, claustrophobic stone shaft of The Dungeon, where he discovers Martin.

Tabitha’s Descent (Season 2): Guided by Victor's memories of his mother's final night, Tabitha Matthews uses a specific Farway Tree to teleport directly to the base of the mysterious Lighthouse in an attempt to save the children trapped in the tower.

Overview
The Bottle Tree is a unique and highly significant variation of the forest's Farway Trees. Located in a secluded clearing, this large tree is easily identifiable by the dozens of glass bottles hanging from its branches by strings. Unlike most Farway Trees, which teleport travelers to completely random coordinates in the woods, the Bottle Tree acts as a stable, fixed portal—always sending whoever enters it to one specific, highly critical destination.

Key Features
The Hanging Bottles: The tree’s branches are heavily draped in glass bottles. Inside these bottles are rolled-up scraps of paper containing written numbers (such as "1864"). Victor’s mother believed these numbers represented the specific years that previous groups of people became trapped in Fromville.

The Fixed Anchor: While standard Farway Trees are volatile and unpredictable, the Bottle Tree serves as a reliable, direct highway to the edge of the Township's boundaries.

Notable Lore
The Lighthouse Gateway (Season 2): When Tabitha Matthews is desperate to find a way to save the "children in the tower," Victor leads her directly to this tree. He reveals that this was the exact location where his mother went on the night of the town massacre. Tabitha climbs into the hollow trunk and is instantly teleported to the base of the mysterious Lighthouse, proving the tree acts as a direct bridge to the tower.

The Mother's Artifact (Season 3): The area surrounding the Bottle Tree holds deep emotional trauma for Victor. It is near this clearing that Victor’s father, Henry, later discovers an old, rusted bicycle belonging to Victor's sister, Eloise—confirming she had chased their mother to this very spot on the night she died.

The Cycle Tracker: The years written on the papers inside the bottles serve as the primary piece of evidence that Fromville operates in distinct, historical cycles, dating back centuries before the current 1950s-era Town was built.

Overview
Located deep within the uncharted woods near a large lake, the Log Cabins are a collection of ancient, decaying wooden structures that completely predate the modern 1950s-era Township. This area is highly atmospheric, heavily overgrown, and serves as a vital but deeply unnerving foraging site for the townspeople due to the wild crops that grow nearby.

Key Features
The Primitive Cabins: A cluster of archaic wooden huts built centuries ago. The architecture suggests that previous generations of trapped travelers attempted to establish a permanent colony here long before the current Town existed.

The Totem Perimeter: The cabins are surrounded by strange, hand-crafted wooden totems. Jade Herrera theorizes that these totems acted as a primitive, early version of the Talismans, used by the old settlers to keep the Creatures away at night.

The Wild Root Fields: The ground surrounding the cabins is one of the few places where crops like potatoes and cabbage grow naturally, making it a necessary destination when the Town's food supplies run low.

Notable Lore
Tabitha’s Dream Connection (Season 1): Upon seeing the cabins, Tabitha Matthews realizes they match a vivid nightmare she had as a child, long before her family ever crossed paths with the tree in the road. This drops the first major hint that the entities running the area can reach out across time and space.

The Iron Spike Vision (Season 2): While exploring the cabins, Jade Herrera is assaulted by a terrifying, localized vision of a man dressed in 1860s-era clothing pinned to the ground with a massive iron spike driven straight through his eye.

The Hidden Bear Trap (Season 2): The surrounding brush hides physical dangers left behind by past eras. During a foraging run, Kristi Miller steps into an ancient, rusted bear trap, forcing Kenny and Jade to perform a tense, grueling emergency extraction to save her leg before nightfall.

Overview
Located on the extreme outskirts of the Town at the very edge of the forest, the Shack is a small, isolated wooden structure. Because it sits far away from the heavily populated zones of the Township, it serves as Fromville's ultimate off-the-grid hideout. When secured with a Talisman, it provides physical safety from the Creatures at night, making it the primary location Boyd Stevens uses to secretly harbor fugitives, exile rule-breakers, or hide traumatized residents from the rest of the community.

Key Features
The Remote Perimeter: Positioned right where the Township ends and the deep woods begin, making it a perfect staging ground or launchpad for dangerous expeditions into the forest.

The Threshold: A small, defensible entry point where a Talisman can be hung, turning a completely exposed structure into a temporary, isolated sanctuary.

Notable Lore
Frank Pratt's Alternative (Season 1): After Frank's negligence led to the brutal deaths of his wife and daughter, Boyd faced the agonizing decision of executing him via "The Box." In a rare act of mercy, Boyd secretly brought Frank a Talisman and told him to flee to this Shack to live out his days in exile. However, consumed by overwhelming grief and guilt, Frank ultimately rejected the offer and chose to accept his execution to be reunited with his family.

Sara's Hidden Staging Ground (Season 1): Following the incident where Sara accidentally killed her brother Nathan, the townspeople believed she had perished in the woods. Boyd secretly used the Shack to hide her from the angry community, using it as a private base to handcuff and prepare her before the two ventured deep into the uncharted forest to find answers.

The Reconciliation of Father and Son (Season 1): While Sara was hidden inside the Shack, Ellis Stevens tracked Boyd to the location. Standing just outside the structure, Ellis finally let go of his years of resentment, tearfully forgiving Boyd for his mother Abby's death and giving his father a proper, emotional goodbye before the forest expedition.

Fatima's Exile & Abduction (Season 3): The Shack became a dark refuge once again after a wave of unnatural, supernatural rage overcame a pregnant Fatima, leading her to accidentally murder Tillie. Boyd and Ellis hid a horrified Fatima inside the Shack with a Talisman to protect her while they figured out a plan. However, the isolation exposed her; after a terrifying vision of the Kimono Woman inside the Shack, Elgin used a photo from the Polaroid camera to track her down, kidnapping her before Boyd and Ellis could return with supplies.

Overview
The Stone Circle is an ancient, deeply unsettling megalithic structure hidden on the outskirts of the Township. It consists of seven large, weathered boulders heavily smeared with an eerie reddish-brown pigment resembling dried blood. Surrounded by primitive, hand-crafted scarecrow totems and stick figures, this landmark completely predates the modern Town. It acts as a major physical manifestation of Fromville's dark history, operating as a localized focal point for spiritual energy and visions.

--

Key Features

The Seven Red Boulders: Massive rocks arranged in a precise circle. The number and orientation of the stones exactly mirror the seven stone slabs found in the deep sacrificial chambers of the subterranean Tunnels.
The Scarecrow Perimeter: Grotesque, life-sized figures fashioned from twigs, burlap, and twine that stand guard around the stone clearing.
The Flattened Center: A perfectly cleared patch of ground inside the ring that remains unaffected by the surrounding forest overgrowth.

--

Notable Lore

Father Khatri’s Sanctuary (Season 1): Long before the town's peace shattered, Father Khatri frequented this clearing to pray, meditate, and contemplate the impossible nature of their reality. He famously marveled at the absolute anomaly of the location, questioning how an ancient European-style pagan structure could physically exist in the middle of a secluded American forest.
The Psychic Conduit: The circle possesses a unique connection to the entities running the Town. It is near this daylight clearing that Father Khatri buried a bag containing a dark secret from his past life—a secret that the forest's malevolent voices were instantly able to detect and manifest through Sara Myers' drawings.
Miranda's Paintings (Season 3): The deeper, generational significance of the site is unmasked through the rediscovered artwork of Victor's mother, Miranda. Decades before the current timeline, Miranda had extensively painted this exact Stone Circle, linking its imagery directly to the spirits of the "Anghkooey" children who are anchored to the stones.

Overview
The Talisman Hut, also known as the Talisman Tomb or Talisman Cave, is a small stone structure hidden deep within the uncharted forest of the Township. This location represents a monumental turning point in the history of Fromville, as it is the exact site where Sheriff Boyd Stevens discovered the stone Talismans that protect the human survivors from the Creatures. Geographically, it serves as the definitive boundary marker between the explored woods and the terrifying, uncharted depths of the forest.

--

Key Features

The Stone Architecture: A naturally protected, enclosed stone chamber or cave structure that is entirely immune to the elements.
The Talisman Vine Pillars: The inner walls of the hut where the protective stone Talismans originally hung, woven into the forest vines before Boyd harvested them for the Town.
The Strategic Waypoint: A localized safety anchor situated precisely where the forest environment begins to change, serving as the last reliable outpost before entering high-risk territory.

--

Notable Lore by Season

Background: The Discovery
While foraging deep in the forest, Boyd Stevens became heavily lost shortly before nightfall. Desperate to find immediate shelter as darkness arrived, he stumbled into this stone cave. He was quickly surrounded by the Creatures, but to his shock, the monsters stood at the threshold and refused to enter. Looking around the interior walls, Boyd discovered the hanging stone artifacts, realizing they possessed a supernatural power to ward off the monsters. He brought them back to the Township, transforming the community from hiding in underground holes to living behind sealed doors.

Season 2: Staging the Forest Expedition
While navigating the woods to find an escape route, Sara Myers asked Boyd how he knew which path to take. Boyd admitted he was merely guessing, but successfully guided her back to the Talisman Cave. Despite having two hours of daylight remaining, Boyd insisted on setting up camp inside the hut for the night, explaining to a skeptical Sara that the cave was the absolute furthest boundary he had ever reached and he refused to push into completely uncharted territory so close to dusk.

Season 3: The Search for Tabitha
Following the disappearance of Tabitha Matthews, Jim Matthews and Deputy Kenny Liu prepared an expedition into the deep woods. Boyd strictly commanded them to locate the Talisman Hut first and use it as a permanent, safe base of operations to sleep in every single night. He gave them navigational markers, explicitly noting that they would know they were heading in the correct direction past the hut when they began encountering massive spiderwebs. Later, while foraging at the distant Log Cabins, Kenny used the location as a strict measurement of time, warning a panicking Jade Herrera that it was too close to dusk and he wouldn't even have enough daylight to make it back to the safety of the Talisman Hut.

Overview
Located on the edges of the Township, this abandoned, rusted-out commercial cargo truck serves as Victor’s deeply private, off-the-grid hideout. While it appears to be mere junk to the rest of the Town, the interior has been entirely retrofitted by Victor over decades of isolation. Because it is small, inconspicuous, and heavily secured with a Talisman at night, it acts as his primary sanctuary where he preserves his childhood belongings, manages his trauma, and hides when the pressures of the community become too overwhelming.

--

Key Features

The Cargo Hold Sanctuary: The enclosed back of the truck, completely packed with Victor’s personal artifacts from the late 1970s, including old blankets, vintage lunchboxes, and childhood relics.
The Drawing Archives: The interior walls are heavily covered with Victor’s crayon drawings, mapping out past events, tragedies, and changing geographical anomalies of the forest.
The Peach Can Stash: A designated storage corner inside the truck where Victor hoards his ultimate comfort food—the town's rare, remaining cans of peaches.

--

Notable Lore

The Safe Space for Trauma: For decades, this truck has been the only place where Victor feels entirely in control of his environment. Having survived the original town-wide massacre alone as a child, the cargo bed acts as a psychological fortress where he can shut out the horrors of the outside world.
The Bond with Ethan (Season 1): Victor brings Ethan Matthews to this hideout, introducing the young boy to his drawings and his collection of toys. It is here that Victor shares his unique perspective on the town’s "Quest," treating Ethan as an intellectual equal who can also see the Boy in White.
The Defense of Privacy: Victor is fiercely protective of this space. As revealed through his interactions with Jade and Tabitha, he experiences severe anxiety and bouts of anger when other residents attempt to go through his things or invade his sanctuary, as it represents the final connection to his lost family.
